primaryReader: Competition law theorist / institutional economist / platform governance researcher
readerProblem: Treating coordination as an ad-hoc privilege rather than establishing non-compensable rights floors that prevent collective coercion.

propositionLedger.statement: Rights floors are strictly non-compensable: material benefits cannot justify the surrender of exit or contestability.
The right to not aggregate (choosing independent outside options) is an equal, protected outcome of the coordination process.
Contestability must operate continuously across proposal formulation, ratification, and pre-execution review.

prohibitedInterpretations: Do not claim coordination rights currently exist in statutory consumer law.
Do not offer legal counsel or compliance advice.
claimBoundary: Conceptual research framework at Evidence Level E0. Non-statutory architectural principles.
handoff: Provides constitutional validation criteria to Module 06 (Travel Stress Test).
